The plan paid $584. The EOB shows $396 as your share: a $250 ER copay plus $146 coinsurance. Because this was emergency care at an out-of-network hospital, special federal protections likely apply, but the document explaining that protection was not available to me, so I am flagging this for a human specialist to confirm you are not overcharged.

lines.explanation: The EOB shows you owe $396 for this ER visit. That is made of two parts. First, a $250 copay — code PR-3 'means this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service' [CODE-PR-3], and your plan says 'The emergency room copay is $250, waived if you are admitted to the hospital' [PLAN-COPAY]. So if you were admitted, this copay should be removed. Second, $146 coinsurance — code PR-2 'means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount' [CODE-PR-2]. The good news: the $1,420 gap between the $2,400 charge and the plan's $980 approved price carries code CO-45, where 'The difference is written off by the provider' [CODE-CO-45] — you should not owe that part. One important note: this was emergency care at an out-of-network hospital. Federal law usually gives you strong protections here, but I was not given the passage that explains that right, so I cannot quote it. A human specialist should confirm your $396 share matches in-network emergency rules and that the hospital cannot bill you for more.

citations.quote: PR-3 means this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service.
The emergency room copay is $250, waived if you are admitted to the hospital.
PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met.
The difference is written off by the provider.

actions: Do not pay anything yet. Wait for the hospital's actual bill, then compare it to this EOB — the member share shown here is $396, and the bill should not ask for more.
If you were admitted to the hospital from the ER, call Sunrise Health member services (number on your ID card) and ask them to remove the $250 copay, since your plan waives it when you are admitted.
Call Sunrise Health member services and ask them to confirm that federal emergency-care protections were applied to this out-of-network ER claim, so the hospital cannot bill you for the difference.
If St. Adelaide Regional Medical Center sends a bill for more than $396, do not pay it — dispute it in writing and contact your plan.
